source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Payment is increasingly tied to the number of billable services delivered, while quality and patient outcomes play a smaller role in financial incentives.","B":"Payment increasingly rewards the quality and outcomes of care rather than service volume alone, aligning financial incentives with better patient care.","C":"Payment removes formal quality measurement from reimbursement decisions, allowing organizations to focus primarily on increasing procedural volume.","D":"Payment separates reimbursement from patient outcomes and care quality, because value-based models are designed only to simplify billing administration."}}
source_row.rationale: CMS describes value-based programs as rewarding quality rather than service quantity alone. Option B captures that shift toward quality and outcomes. Option A describes the volume emphasis of fee-for-service rather than the intended value-based direction. Option C incorrectly removes quality measurement from reimbursement. Option D incorrectly separates payment from quality and outcomes.
source_row.source_detail: CMS — Value-Based Programs: value-based programs reward health care providers with incentive payments for quality of care and move payment toward quality rather than quantity/service volume alone. CMS Value-Based Programs page modified 2026-03-10; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A health system shifts from fee-for-service toward value-based payment. Which statement best describes the intended change?
